newsitem.title: JAPAN: SOCCER-LIPPI PRAISES HIS JUVENTUS WINNERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LIPPI PRAISES HIS JUVENTUS WINNERS.

text.p: Juventus won the World Club Cup final for the second time in their history on Tuesday when an 82nd-minute goal from Alessandro Del Piero gave them a 1-0 win over River Plate of Argentina.
The Italians, playing with seven of the men who won the European Cup final in May, had the better of a scrappy match and undoubtedly deserved to win.
They won praise from their coach Marcello Lippi afterwards.
Lippi, who has rebuilt the side since Juventus were crowned European champions, said: "We were able to play to our own rhythm and I think we dominated the match.
"We worked hard for three years to bring ourslves up to this level and I think everybody in the team deserves credit for this championship."
River Plate manager Ramon Diaz said: "Both teams played extremely well and I am satisfied the way we played today. I hope we can come back again to Tokyo next year."

The victory sparked celebrations in the streets of Turin, with fans gathering in the main square to cheer the Italian success and others in cars forming a procession in the streets, flying Juve flags outside the windows.
The winning goal came eight minutes from time when Angelo Di Livio's corner was flicked on to Del Piero lurking unmarked on the far side of the box.

The 22-year-old striker turned and controlled the ball and in the same movement sent it soaring past River Plate goalkeeper Roberto Bonano who had no chance of stopping it flying past his left-hand shoulder into the far corner of the the net.

The goal belatedly brought what had been a competitive but scrappy match to life and Croatian striker Alen Boksic, a new addition to the side since May, had two good chances to score after trademark Juve counter-attacks but wasted them both.

Boksic also should have done better after 55 minutes when Del Piero provided him with a beautifully weighted ball inside the River Plate box. But the Croat failed to connect properly and sent a weak side-footed effort straight at the goalkeeper.
Whenever River Plate threatened the Juventus goal, Uruguayan defender Paolo Montero and the long-haired Moreno Torricelli were quick to close the attackers down.

But the Italians were fortunate after 38 minutes when veteran Uruguayan international Enzo Francescoli found himself with time and space at the edge of the penalty area. But Francescoli rushed his effort and sent a left-foot volley flying high and wide of Angelo Peruzzi's goal.
River Plate went close at the other end in the later stages but the nearest they came to a goal was when Ariel Ortego hit the crossbar from an acute angle after 72 minutes.

Juventus followed Ajax's success for Europe in this final last year. Since the competition began in 1960, South American sides have won it 20 times against Europe's 15. Juventus's previous victory came in 1985 when they beat Argentinos Juniors on penalties.

Juventus: 1-Angelo Peruzzi; 2-Ciro Ferrara, 5-Sergio Porrini, 3-Moreno Torricelli, 4-Paolo Montero, 7-Angelo Di Livio, 14-Didier Deschamps, 18-Vladimir Jugovic, 21-Zinedine Zidane (20-Alessio Tacchinardi 86), 10-Alessandro Del Piero, 9-Alen Boksic

River Plate: 1-Roberto Bonano; 4-Hernan Diaz, 6-Eduardo Berizzo, 2-Celso Ayala, 3-Juan Sorin, 5-Leonardo Astrada, 8-Roberto Montserrat, 11-Sergio Berti (18-Leonel Gancedo 75), 10-Ariel Ortega, 9-Enzo Francescoli, 7-Julio Cruz (Marcelo Salas 84) .
